name: Dravanet Pecs Data Center
notes: DatacenterPlatform lists Dravanet Zrt. (HQ Pecs, Baranya) with a colocation data center at Budai Nagy Antal u. 1, 7624 Pecs and a total of 3 data centers (Pecs plus regional sites). Dravanet's official site (dravanet.hu) confirms it is the regional telecom/ICT operator offering server hosting and VPS. Facility existence rests on directory listings; no operator facility page with DC specs or MW was found.

name: Magyar Telekom Dataplex / T-Systems Cloud & DataCenter (Asztalos Sandor u.)
notes: Magyar Telekom's official wholesale hosting page lists T-Systems Cloud & DataCenter at 1087 Budapest, Asztalos Sandor u. 13 (corner of Ciprus utca). ComputerTrends confirms T-Systems operates four data centers in Hungary: two in Budapest (Adatpark and Dataplex) plus Gyor and Szeged. Commercial colocation/hosting. Baxtel market summary claims ~8 MW for Dataplex (unverified capacity, kept null).

name: Magyar Telekom Victor Hugo DC
notes: Telekom's official hosting page lists Victor Hugo DC at 1132 Budapest, Victor Hugo utca 18-22; the building hosts the BIX (Budapest Internet Exchange) ecosystem with multiple operators (e.g. hostit.hu colocation at 'BIX epulet', 1132 Budapest Victor Hugo 18-22). Commercial colocation/telecom datacenter. Capacity not publicly disclosed.

name: RackForest / Rackhost Data Center (Victor Hugo utca)
notes: Rendszerinformatika's official Victor Hugo datacenter page lists 1132 Budapest, Victor Hugo 18-22, 70 rack spaces, 270 sqm gross, 3 kW per rack (~0.21 MW). RackForest's official service page states georedundancy across 5 server rooms and 3 Budapest locations. Commercial hosting/colocation.

name: VIVAnet Data Center Budapest
notes: Official VIVAnet page: carrier-neutral data center in the heart of Budapest, operating since July 2024; first-phase room built for 140 rack cabinets. Commercial colocation. No public MW figure.

name: Servergarden / Systech Ilka utcai adatkozpont
notes: Systech Global's official Ilka utcai adatkozpont page (Budapest XIV district) provides facility/network/cooling/security details; Systech also lists a Kozma utcai server room (1108 Budapest, Kozma utca 2 - Dataneum building shared with Invitech DC10). DataCenterJournal lists Servergarden as operating its Budapest facility (DoclerNet, ~25,457 sq ft). Commercial hosting/colocation.

name: Invitech DC10 / Dataneum (Kozma utca 2)
notes: DatacenterPlatform lists Invitech DC10 at Kozma u. 2, 1108 Budapest (X district); Inflect reports ~2,000 kW capacity; Uptime Institute lists Invitech Solutions DC10-III Budapest. 2Connect (formed from Antenna Hungaria, DIGI, Invitech and Vodafone HU network units) officially claims 6,500+ sqm of data center capacity across 12 sites (3 commercial, 9 telecom). Some directory listings alias DC10 to Budaors; the primary physical address here is Budapest X district.

name: Wigner Data Centre (CERN remote Tier-0 extension)
developer: HUN-REN Wigner Research Centre for Physics / CERN
notes: CERN primary press release (2013-06-13): Wigner Data Centre in Budapest inaugurated as extension of CERN computing resources with about 500 servers, 20,000 computing cores, 5.5 PB storage. Wigner states the data centre was built with 4 MW IT capacity and 2x100 Gbit/s connection to CERN, hosting CERN Tier-0 equipment since January 2013. Research/HPC facility, not commercial colo. 4 MW capacity claim kept in notes (B-grade corroboration).

name: NISZ Kormanyzati Adatkozpont (KAK) Budapest
notes: Press reports: new unified, cloud-based Kormanyzati Adatkozpont (KAK) built in Budapest for >16 billion HUF, delivering hosting/IaaS/PaaS/SaaS for government; digitrendi.hu reported the new government datacenter completed in Budapest. Government Decree 467/2017 (XII. 28.) regulates Kormanyzati Adatkozpont operation. Public-sector datacenter; capacity not disclosed. Press B + regulation A.

name: University of Miskolc HPC / supercomputer
notes: 24.hu (2015-10-25) reports a new supercomputer at the University of Miskolc (1.5 TB RAM, 240 TB storage) funded by EU money; KIFU HPC history page (hpc.unideb.hu/tortenet) confirms an HPC machine was commissioned at the University of Miskolc in late 2015. Research/HPC facility in Miskolc, Borsod-Abauj-Zemplen county; not commercial colocation. MW not disclosed.

name: Magyar Telekom Adatpark Szeged
notes: Magyar Telekom's official wholesale hosting page lists Adatpark Szeged at 6724 Szeged, Rokusi krt. 2-10 among its data centers (with Budapest and Gyor). Commercial colocation/hosting. No public MW figure.

name: Rackhost Data Center Szeged
notes: DataCenterMap states Rackhost Data Center Szeged was established in 2011 in the telecommunications hub at Tisza Lajos krt. 41, with redundant high-speed connections to the Budapest Data Center and Telekom Dataplex. Directory-grade facility lead; Rackhost official site confirms the hosting provider. No public MW figure.

name: University of Szeged / Komondor HPC ecosystem
notes: University of Szeged news describes the Komondor supercomputer being hosted/used in Szeged research infrastructure as part of the national HPC (KIFU) ecosystem. Research/HPC compute facility, separate from commercial colocation. No MW figure.

name: DP Data Center (Galamb utca 1)
developer: Dryvit Profi Kft. / DP Data Center
notes: EPS-Connect reported (2021) a unique commercial datacenter being built in Debrecen's Galamb utca office building by Dryvit Profi, designed for direct water cooling and high-density racks; Dryvit Profi's own post describes DP Data Center server-centre construction. datacenter.hu markets the DP Data Center brand. Current operational status and MW not confirmed in accessible public sources; status kept as construction per 2021 report.

name: BMW Group Plant Debrecen DC1 datacenter optical connection
developer: BMW Hungary Kft. / Invitech ICT Services
notes: NMHH official telecom-construction notice (decision CD60532/2023) granted a building permit for the optical connection of BMW Hungary Kft. DC1 datacenter in Debrecen - grade A official evidence of datacenter infrastructure inside the BMW plant campus; Invitech/DCD report the optical delivery for the plant's DC1 node. Enterprise/campus server infrastructure, not independent colocation. BMW plant itself entered production in late 2025; DC1 status per 2023 permit kept as construction.

name: Komondor Supercomputer Center (University of Debrecen)
notes: KIFU/University of Debrecen: 5-petaflop Komondor supercomputer installed at the Kassai Street campus in summer 2023 in the national HPC centre, maximum electrical power 500 kW (0.5 MW). Research/HPC facility, separate from commercial colo.

name: DC Hosting / Data Center Solutions Kft. (Eger)
notes: Data Center Solutions Kft. (DC Hosting) is an Eger-based (3300 Eger, Kodaly Zoltan utca 6; Cifrakapu utca 162) RIPE LIR and PeeringDB-registered operator with own ASN AS210966, offering datacenter/server hosting services; domain.hu lists it as a .hu registrar. Operator identity is well documented (RIPE/PeeringDB), but no public facility page with DC specs or capacity was found - C for facility existence.

name: MH OHP / Szekesfehervar military IT server room
developer: Hungarian Defence Forces (contractor: Klimagaz Hungary Kft.)
notes: Contractor (Klimagaz) reference list includes 'Informatikai szerverterem Szfv' (IT server room, Szekesfehervar, Fejer county) and 'MH OHP Szerverterem' military server-room project with 200 kW DX cooling. Small public-sector/enterprise server room, not commercial colocation; no IT load or commissioning date in public source. C-grade contractor reference.

name: Magyar Telekom Adatpark Gyor
notes: Magyar Telekom's official wholesale hosting page lists Adatpark Gyor at 9021 Gyor, Teleki Laszlo u. 36 among its four Hungarian data centers (Budapest x2, Gyor, Szeged). County-level entry for Gyor-Moson-Sopron. No public MW figure.

name: Magyar Telekom Adatpark Gyor
notes: Same facility recorded at city level: Magyar Telekom Adatpark Gyor (9021 Gyor, Teleki Laszlo u. 36) confirmed by official Telekom hosting page and DC Byte (colocation retail, Magyar Telekom). Capacity not disclosed.
